name: section-cycle-error-chain
body: A declared-section reference cycle is a templates error naming the chain, e.g. `sections/a → sections/b → sections/a`, unless a declaration on the cycle carries `max_depth: N`: then the cycle is bounded self-nesting (requirements.requirement.bounded-self-nesting), the loader walks the declaration graph bounded by max_depth, and the cycle is valid. A reference is a declared `sections:` acceptance, a `section` helper call in a layout, or a `child` constructor's template target (section-helper-load-checks, child-constructor); a helper- or child-closed cycle carries no declared max_depth and is rejected exactly like an unbounded declared one. A cycle no declaration bounds is never accepted (the composition walk terminates safely and reports the chain instead of looping), and it is a templates error path-qualified to the offending `template.yaml` (template-build-checks).
